verdict: Oracle's revenue grew 14% to $16.1B as cloud revenue jumped 34% — and a $2.7B gain from selling its Ampere chip stake lifted net income 95% to $6.1B.

kpis.label: Ampere gain
kpis.note: one-time, on selling its chip company stake

segments.name: Cloud
segments.note: Cloud infrastructure (OCI) revenue of $4.1B grew 68%, and cloud applications (SaaS) brought in $3.9B, up 11% — now 50% of all revenue.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Traditional software licenses and support — shrinking slightly as customers migrate to the cloud.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software — up 4% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to enterprises — down 2% YoY despite the growth push.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, up 6% YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge, down 31% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Restructuring charges of $406M — nearly five times a year ago — plus $21M of acquisition-related costs.

takeaways.title: The backlog exploded
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations hit $523B, up 438% in a year and up $68B in the quarter — highlighted by new commitments from Meta and NVIDIA. Years of cloud revenue are already signed.

takeaways.title: Infrastructure is the engine
takeaways.text: Cloud infrastructure (OCI) revenue grew 68% to $4.1B; total cloud revenue was $8.0B, up 34% and now half of everything Oracle earns.

takeaways.title: A one-time gain did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Selling Oracle's stake in chip designer Ampere added a $2.7B pre-tax gain. Operating income was $4.7B, up 12%, and the tax bill was just $207M — together they explain why net income nearly doubled.

oneTimers: A $2.7B pre-tax gain on the sale of Oracle's stake in Ampere Computing, its chip-design company — it sits inside the $2,668M of net non-operating income.
Restructuring charges of $406M — nearly five times the $84M of a year ago — sit inside operating expenses.
otherDetail: Non-operating income of $2,668M — mostly the $2.7B pre-tax gain on the sale of Oracle's Ampere chip stake — partly offset by $1,057M of interest expense on Oracle's growing debt pile.
footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud and software', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue.
